item.title: Liquidity in Malaysia May Tighten Further as Rate-Hike Bets Grow
item.description: Funding conditions in Malaysia’s money market will likely tighten further later this year, with some analysts expecting stronger economic growth to prompt the country’s central bank to raise interest rates.

item.title: Yen Options Suggest a Slide to 165 Level Before Japan Intervenes
item.description: The yen has room to weaken more before Japanese officials step in to support the currency, options suggest.

item.title: Global Investors Hunt For Creative Backdoors Into China’s Mega CXMT IPO
item.description: Global investors largely shut out of China’s biggest IPO in nearly four years are looking at creative proxy trades as a way to profit from the country’s fast-rising memory-chip leader.

item.title: Iran War Drives New Investment in US LNG, S&P Global Says
item.description: The Iran war, and its disruptions across global energy markets, is spurring investments for new US liquefied natural gas export infrastructure, according to consulting firm S&P Global.

item.title: Li Ka-shing’s Cash-Out Plan Sets Up Empire for Leadership Shift
item.description: Billionaire Li Ka-shing and his family are preparing to usher in a new generation of leaders after some of their longest-serving lieutenants wrap up the sale of various assets to overhaul Hong Kong’s largest conglomerate.

item.title: Nvidia Expands Toyota AI Partnership for Smart Cities, Factories
item.description: Nvidia Corp. will supply its artificial intelligence hardware and software to Toyota Motor Corp. to power smart cities, traffic intelligence systems and carmaking factories, broadening a decade-long partnership that began with developing autonomous vehicles.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Soft Inflation, War Risk Cloud Fed Rate Outlook
item.description: Gold steadied, as traders weighed softer-than-expected inflation data against escalating attacks in the Middle East for clues to the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

item.title: BHP’s Iron Ore, Copper Output Slip as Miner Plans for Growth
item.description: BHP Group Ltd.’s iron ore production fell in the three months through June as the miner pushes ahead with expansions in copper and potash.

item.title: Data Center Firm Csquare Is Said to Price IPO at $21 Per Share
item.description: Csquare Inc. priced its initial public offering at $21 per share, according to people familiar with the matter, below a marketed range.

item.title: Oil Advances on Iran, Stocks Set for Mixed Open: Markets Wrap
item.description: Crude oil extended gains as the US launched fresh strikes on Iran, raising concerns that Middle East tensions will further disrupt energy supplies. Stocks in Asia are set to open mixed.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 16
item.description: Oil climbed for a fourth day as the US continued its attacks on Iran in a bid to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: China Sends Robots Out Into the World to Learn How to Be Human
item.description: In an industrial park on the outskirts of Beijing, a humanoid arm picks up a bag of Lay’s potato chips and places it neatly along a row of snacks on a shelf. Nearby, a worker films himself grabbing cushions off a sofa and folding sheets on a bed, recording videos that will be used to develop brains for robots.

item.title: JPMorgan Leads $3 Billion Financing for Warburg’s Pantherx Buy
item.description: A group of lenders led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. is lining up a debt package worth up to $3 billion to support Warburg Pincus’ acquisition of Pantherx Specialty LLC, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: The Optimistic Case for the Hochul Data Center Pause
item.description: All politicians are being forced to navigate this issue.

item.title: Pool Stocks Sink as Consumers Cautious Despite Scorching Summer
item.description: Shares of companies in the swimming pool business sank on Wednesday amid signs that wary consumers are pulling back on spending despite a summer of intense heat.

item.title: Brazil to Offer Billions in Debt Relief for Struggling Farmers
item.description: Brazil’s government plans to publish a provisional measure on Wednesday to renegotiate more than 100 billion reais ($20 billion) in rural debt, as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva prepares to seek reelection in October.

item.title: Short-Sellers Swarm SpaceX With Paper Profit Nearing $4 Billion
item.description: SpaceX bears are minting billions on paper as the company’s stock price cracks ahead of a closely-watched rocket launch and upcoming earnings that will unlock a flood of shares.

item.title: Regional Banks, Wealth Management Lead Financial Services M&A
item.description: Smaller deals involving regional banks and wealth managers are driving acquisitions in the financial services industry, according to a clutch of industry watchers.

item.title: Apple Boosts AppleCare+ Monthly Prices by 50 Cents in Latest Increase
item.description: Apple Inc. slightly raised the cost of individual AppleCare+ service subscriptions, marking its latest price increase in the face of a global memory shortage and other challenges.

item.title: Kalshi Seeks to Let Traders Bet on Flight Cancellation Rates
item.description: Your flight? Canceled. The silver lining? You might be able to make some money off the misery.

item.title: Fed’s Beige Book Shows Slight to Moderate Growth Across US
item.description: US economic activity increased at a slight to moderate pace in recent weeks as most regions experienced little to no change in employment levels, the Federal Reserve said.

item.title: Murati’s Thinking Machines Releases First AI Model for Broad Use
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab is releasing its first AI model, more than a year after former OpenAI executive Mira Murati founded the artificial intelligence startup.

item.title: SpaceX IPO Lifts Wall Street ECM Revenue to Best Since 2021
item.description: Wall Street’s biggest investment banks hauled in the most revenue from advising on equity offerings in the second quarter since 2021, fueled by SpaceX’s record-setting IPO and a fundraising blitz for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Airbus Set to Win A330 Jet Deals from Flynas, Condor
item.description: Airbus SE is in talks to sell more of its A330neo widebody aircraft to Saudi low-cost carrier Flynas Co SJSC and German airline Condor Flugdienst GmbH.

item.title: Palantir’s CTO Sees Chinese AI Models Posing Economic Risk to US
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. Chief Technology Officer Shyam Sankar said that China has developed a new vanguard of artificial intelligence models through unauthorized use of work produced by Silicon Valley AI developers, posing an economic threat to the US.

item.title: Iran’s Tanker Attacks Squeeze the Hormuz Oil-Shuttling Trade
item.description: Iran’s recent attacks on oil tankers are jeopardizing an innovative trade that has rapidly expanded in recent months to become one of the main ways for getting crude out of the Persian Gulf — so-called “shuttle runs.”

item.title: Lead Prices Slump as Trafigura Lifts LME Stockpiles to a Record
item.description: Lead prices fell toward the lowest since 2022 after Trafigura Group made a second record-breaking delivery of metal into London Metal Exchange warehouses.

item.title: CIA Says AI Drones Give Russian Troops Only 30 Minutes to Live
item.description: Russian soldiers only live an average of 20 to 30 minutes on the battlefield because of Ukraine’s artificial-intelligence attack drones, CIA Director John Ratcliffe said on Wednesday.

item.title: Saudi Gulf Oil Loads Slump as Iran Hits Tankers in Hormuz
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s oil loadings from inside the Persian Gulf have slumped in the wake of an upsurge of attacks on supertankers in the Strait of Hormuz, satellite images reviewed by Bloomberg show, demonstrating how Iran is once again disrupting supply.

item.title: Fed’s Cook Says Prepared to Act If Inflation Doesn’t Cool
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the risk of persistent inflation now outweighs that of a weakening labor market, as the artificial-intelligence build-out and recent supply shocks drive price pressures.
